description: Interactive spreadsheets — cell grids with text, formatting, and formulas, optionally with assessed cells that grade what a learner types. Describe the layout, the cells, the formulas, and any grading rules.

example_prompts.prompt: Create a four-column spreadsheet with a header row (Product, Qty, Unit Price, Line Total), 3 data rows with =B*C line totals in column D, and a SUM grand total under column D. Bold the header row.
example_prompts.notes: Names the columns, the per-row formula, and the total — the backend places cells by address without having to infer the layout.

example_prompts.prompt: Create a 3 by 3 grid of assessed input cells where the expected answers are 1 through 9, reading left to right, top to bottom.
example_prompts.notes: States the fill order explicitly, which is what maps expected answers onto addresses.

example_prompts.prompt: Put values 10, 20, and 30 in A1 through A3. Assess cell A4 expecting the student to enter the formula =SUM(A1:A3).
example_prompts.notes: A formula expectation is re-evaluated against the current cell values at scoring time, so it stays correct when the inputs are parameterized.

example_prompts.prompt: Create a payroll check sheet with headers Employee, Hours, Rate, Gross Pay. Three rows of data. Column D is blank and assessed by value, expecting the computed gross pay, worth 2 points per cell.
example_prompts.notes: Per-cell points are set with `points` on the cell's assess list; omitting it means 1 point. Each assessed cell scores independently, so partial credit needs no special request.

example_prompts.prompt: Create a parameterized spreadsheet where A1 and A2 are filled from params holding two rainfall readings, and A3 is an assessed cell expecting their total.
example_prompts.notes: Param keys are quoted cell addresses; a cell reads one with {{NAME}}. Values may be a choice list or a start..stop:step range.

example_prompts.prompt: Create a two-column label/value layout with 4 rows. Column A has bold labels; column B is right-aligned with a light-yellow background. The last row computes a SUM of the rows above.
example_prompts.notes: Formatting stated per column is applied to the column rather than repeated on every cell.

example_prompts.prompt: Create a worksheet listing water samples with pH values, and a Status column using an IF formula that shows Pass when the pH is at least 6.5 and Fail otherwise.
example_prompts.notes: IF, SUM, AVERAGE, ROUND, POWER, MAX, MIN, ABS and arithmetic are the available formula functions; naming the comparison spells out the condition.
